feedback.problem:
The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=3,{x}_{3}=4,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,-$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,+$
{{field-3}}$x\,-$
{{field-4}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=3,$ ${x}_{2}=3,$ and ${x}_{3}=4,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-3)(x-3)(x-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-3)(x-3)(x-4) & =2({x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-6{x}^{2}+24x+9x-36) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-10{x}^{2}+33x-36) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-20{x}^{2}+66x-72.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-20{x}^{2}+66x-72.$
